title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure, and it sits at the very front of the transaction, in the advertisement that persuaded the victim to pay anything at all. A synthetic video presented a well-known figure from the finance industry as the face of an investment offer, and the victim's decision to make a first small payment followed from believing that person stood behind it. The false element was not a wrong number or a bad forecast, it was the identity of the party making the offer.

The fraud did not depend on the video alone. Once the first payment was made, contact moved to WhatsApp, the victim was pressed to send more, was told to borrow money, and was induced to open several online accounts and hand remote control of their computer to the criminals, who framed this as help with the investment. The £250,000 loss accumulated across that later stage. Police pointed to two checks that would have interrupted it, confirming who the victim was actually dealing with and confirming that the financial services provider was authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority.

What is not established is who the impersonated figure was, since police did not name them, and no arrest, charge or verdict appears in the reporting. BBC News NI having seen other scams that use finance experts does not show that any of those people endorsed this offer or had any part in it.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in Ards and north Down lost £250,000 after an AI video scam. The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the victim watched a fake video that seemed to show a famous person from the finance industry. It advertised an investment and promised large profits. After a small first payment, the victim was contacted on WhatsApp and pushed to send more. The criminals had the victim set up several online accounts and took remote control of their computer, claiming to help with the investment. Police described the case as a complex and large fraud.

Police did not name the celebrity. BBC News NI has seen scams that use finance experts such as Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett. The victim was told to borrow money, and the funds went to accounts run by criminals. Superintendent Joanne Gibson of the Scamwise Partnership urged people to pause and check financial activity and for families to discuss fraud. Police advised people to confirm who they are dealing with and check that financial services providers are authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority.
